title: What If a Giant Asteroid Flew Closer Than Our Satellites?

scenes.text: What if a giant asteroid flew closer than our satellites? In 2029, one will.
It is called Apophis, about 375 meters across, and it was found in 2004.
When astronomers first calculated its path, they gave a 2.7 percent chance of hitting Earth in 2029.
Radar in 2021 ruled out any impact for at least 100 years. Instead, it will pass within 32,000 kilometers.
That is inside the ring of geostationary satellites, 36,000 kilometers up. People in Europe, Africa and Asia could see it with the naked eye.
NASA is sending a spacecraft to study it. A near miss, turned into a free lesson in how to defend Earth.

description:
What if a giant asteroid flew closer to Earth than our satellites?
Apophis will do exactly that on April 13, 2029, and impact has been ruled out for at least 100 years.
What should we run through next?
